evidence: No test scans src/proof for network use. design.md (Test strategy, Offline) promises a source scan for node:http, node:https, node:net, node:tls, node:dgram and fetch, but tests/proof/unit/sourceScan.test.ts checks only process.env and console/stdio. A grep of src/proof found no such call today. A test would walk src/proof and fail on those imports and on fetch calls (the same test covers 16.1).

tests/proof/unit/orchestrator.test.ts asserts original.verified and original.integrity, but no test asserts that report.package holds the Original name and exact version. A test would run runProofOfLife and compare report.package with the request's original name and version.

PREEXISTING.md lists tar 7.5.23 with chownr, minipass, yallist, @isaacs/fs-minipass and minizlib, each with license and source URL, and the D9 note on BlueOak-1.0.0. A grep of src and scripts shows only src/proof/shell/tarball/tarballExtractor.ts imports tar; no test enforces it (see 3.8).

No test fails when a file under src/proof other than src/proof/shell/tarball/tarballExtractor.ts imports tar (tests/proof/integration/lodashBroken.integration.test.ts imports tar for its own use, which is outside src/proof). A test would scan src/proof for imports of tar and allow only the extractor.

README.md 'Known limitations' states that ESM is not supported and describes the undetected case (L12). design.md 'unloadable-module detection' states that R3.11 forbids claiming ES module support. A package with type module is rejected as unloadable-module (tests/proof/unit/orchestrator.test.ts, 'type module' case).

design.md section 'Known limitations', item L1 (reference identity), states the consequence for argument aliasing and for functions that return their arguments. README.md 'Known limitations' repeats L1 in short form.

src/proof/core/equal.ts imports only the codec and types, and the determinism lint (tests/proof/unit/determinismLint.test.ts, cited 16.2) bans Date.now, new Date() and Math.random in core, but no test checks that the comparison modules import no node:fs or clock. A test would scan the imports of src/proof/core/equal.ts and its codec dependencies for node:fs and clock access.

No test runs a setup module before the package loads. orchestrator.test.ts only validates that setupModule is an absolute path, and protocol.test.ts only round-trips the load message. A test would give a harness a setupModule that stubs a value, open both sides through a real executor and check that the package sees the stub on each side.

The ip harness is out of scope (16.6) and nothing replaces os.networkInterfaces through a setup module in any test or harness. The same setup-module test as 8.9, with a setup module that replaces os.networkInterfaces, would show it applied identically to both sides.

README.md 'Known limitations' states that an unbounded .filter hangs the run and cannot be detected (L13), and gives the rule for harness authors. The criterion itself says the rule is enforced by code review and the runner timeout, so no engine behavior is tested.

tests/proof/integration/lodashBroken.integration.test.ts asserts Replay_Parameters, both Outcomes and the shrink fields of a divergence, and tests/proof/unit/report.test.ts asserts redactionMaskedDifference, but no test asserts that report.seed equals the harness Seed. A test would run runProofOfLife with a fixed seed and compare report.seed.

tests/proof/unit/report.test.ts only passes injected toolVersions through buildReport and checks reportSchema 1. No test asserts that defaultProofDeps() reads process.version and the fast-check version at run time. A test would compare defaultProofDeps().toolVersions with process.version and the installed fast-check version.

docs/proof-of-life-ordering.md: sections 'Key order' (top level and nested tables, position of unencodableValues), 'List ordering', 'Divergence sort' (redacted counterexample), 'Divergence shape and redactionMaskedDifference' and 'Unencodable reasons' (code point order of reasons keys).

tests/proof/unit/normalize.test.ts and tempRootLeak.test.ts exercise the redaction, and tempRootLeak.test.ts loops over both sides, but no test states that the Path_Redactor is a pure function of text and roots or that both sides get the same treatment. A test would call it twice on equal inputs (inputs unchanged, equal outputs) and compare the output for the Original and Resurrection with swapped roots.

tests/proof/unit/tempRootLeak.test.ts (serialized report and temp roots) and endToEndIdentity.test.ts (home path) cover two of the three. No test builds a serialized report from an error message holding the Node installation directory and checks the text; normalize.test.ts checks the Node directory only on redactErrorText. A test would run the report builder with such a message and assert the serialized text lacks the directory.

PREEXISTING.md lists tar with chownr, minipass, yallist, @isaacs/fs-minipass and minizlib, and the lodash.set@4.3.2 tarball (section 'Third-party material in test fixtures'), with license and source. .kiro/steering/necromancy-laws.md states that the MIT/ISC/BSD/Apache-2.0 list applies to resurrected packages and that project dependencies may use BlueOak-1.0.0.

tests/engine/helpers/fc.test.ts asserts numRuns >= 100 for the shared fcParams(), which the proof property tests use (p24 and p24b take max(100, fcParams().numRuns)). The covering file lives under tests/engine and cites the autopsy-engine numbering (12.5), so no proof-of-life-engine header was added.

docs/kiro-journal.md records user-run wall-clock figures for proof-property and proof-integration (for example the entry with 'proof-integration: 49.6 s (target 120 s)'). tests/proof/helpers/budgetGlobalSetup.ts sets the budgets at 60 s and 120 s.

tests/proof/helpers/budgetGlobalSetup.ts fails the run or warns (PROOF_BUDGET_MODE=warn) when a project exceeds its target, and docs/kiro-journal.md records runs that failed with '... over the 60 s target'. No automated test exercises the overrun branch. A test would call the budget check with a fake elapsed time above the target in both modes.

tests/engine/unit/networkGuard.test.ts (network blocked in every project through the root setupFiles) and tests/engine/helpers/fc.test.ts ('uses FC_SEED when set') assert it. Both files live under tests/engine and cite the autopsy-engine numbering, so no proof-of-life-engine header was added.

Same gap as 1.6: tests/setup/networkGuard.ts blocks network access while tests run, but no test scans src/proof for LLM or network calls outside scripts/lib/recordTarball.ts. A grep of src/proof found none today. A test would scan src/proof for network imports, fetch and LLM client packages.

Scope exclusions (no attestation signing, pull requests, Kiro agents, native addons) have no test; a grep of src/proof found no such code. Cycles stay unencodable (codec.test.ts cites 6.x) and a type module package is rejected as unloadable-module (orchestrator.test.ts). A source scan test, extending the one for 1.6 and 16.1, would fail on imports of an attestation or GitHub client, Kiro, or a .node addon load.

design.md: the ProofRequest comment 'Reserved for D4 (read-only dependency root)' (the strict schema rejects a dependencyRoot key), the ip harness section naming SideSpec.readPaths as the extension point, and the 'Deliberately not tested' list ('The ip harness (design hook only)'). src/proof contains no dependency root or ip harness.
